notes: 2026-08-30 (branch `fix/destructive-endpoint-guards`, off master 6c8f1401; no schema change) — HARDENED TWO DESTRUCTIVE ENDPOINTS. B126: `DELETE /settings/financial-data` (`settings.controller.ts`) was an unscoped `deleteMany({})` across the finance models, wiping EVERY tenant's finances from one call with no confirmation — irreversible and cross-tenant. B127: `customers.service.ts deleteAllCustomers` had no PAID/SENT invoice guard, unlike its sibling `batchDelete`, so it would destroy paid invoices its neighbor refuses to touch. Fixed: B126 now refuses a null tenant (`ForbiddenException`), requires a typed `ClearFinancialDataDto.confirmTenantId === caller's own tenantId` (`BadRequestException` otherwise), and scopes every delete explicitly — parents on `where: { tenantId }`, children on a RELATION filter over the parent's tenantId (`{ invoice: { tenantId } }`, `{ vendorBill: … }`, `{ po: … }`, `{ creditNote: … }`), because finance child rows are nullable-tenant and nested-created children carry `tenantId: null`. Missing them is fatal, not untidy: `InvoicePayment.invoiceId`, `BillPayment.vendorBillId` and `OrderCreditNote.creditNoteId` are ON DELETE RESTRICT, so one surviving NULL-tenant child aborts its parent's delete (P2003) and rolls the whole wipe back — `orderCreditNote` was added to the cleared set for exactly that reason. B127 now runs the same PAID/SENT pre-flight as `batchDelete` before any deletion, and — since `DELETE /customers/all` is reachable by SUPER_ADMIN — refuses a null tenant the same way B126 does, so the listing, the pre-flight and the wipe can never span every tenant; its blocker breakdown is capped at 10 + "and N more" because, unlike `batchDelete`'s, the list is every customer in the tenant. Durable lesson — `tenantTransaction` misleads in BOTH directions: with a null tenant it hands back the raw client (`prisma.service.ts` `if (!tenantId) return fn(rawTx)`), a pass-through and not a guard; with a tenant it hands back `_wrapTxWithTenant`, which lists `deleteMany` in `SCOPED_METHODS` and rewrites EVERY call as `where: { ...args.where, tenantId }`, silently re-scoping a deliberate parent-scoped child filter onto the child's own (null) tenantId. So this wipe runs on `prisma.$transaction`, not `tenantTransaction`; mocks hide the injection, so the B126 spec's fake calls the REAL `_wrapTxWithTenant`. KNOWN LIMITATION, unchanged: `CommissionAccrual.invoiceId` is also RESTRICT and is NOT cleared, so a tenant holding commission accruals still fails this wipe on that FK. Specs: `settings.controller.clear-financial.spec.ts`, `customers.service.delete-all.spec.ts`. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
